I've been working this same rotation for three decades on the North China Plain, so I know what this land needs. My 10.1 mu runs wheat and maize on the same fields year-round — wheat goes in October, comes out June, then maize straight into June through October. Both crops cover the full plot.

With two of us in the household and my son working in the city, I have to keep labor manageable. But I've also had enough schooling and enough seasons to know where I can't cut corners.

**Wheat:** I'll use Jimai 22 — it's proven in this county, good lodging resistance, and I know its quirks. I plough in rotary after maize harvest to break up the compaction layer and incorporate the stubble. I fertilize at sowing with compound base fertilizer, then topdress nitrogen at jointing — that's where the yield is built. Three irrigations: sowing water to get establishment, jointing water, and one at anthesis if it's dry. Three pesticide passes: seed dressing, post-emergence herbicide in November, and a fungicide at heading to keep scab and rust off. I expect around 500 kg/mu on my fields.

**Maize:** I plant hybrid seed right after wheat harvest — no-till straight in, machine seeding, which saves me days of labor in the summer heat. Maize is hungry for nitrogen so I go heavier there, side-dressing at V6 and again at tasseling. I'll irrigate at sowing if the soil is too dry, and again at silking — that's the critical window. Two pesticide applications: herbicide early, then watch for corn borer and spray if pressure is there. I'm targeting 600 kg/mu.
